segments: The 11th {OCR? reading: ܝܝ for ܝܐ?} dynasty:
The Arab kings.
[Mahmud the son of] Malik-Shah {OCR?} as sultan in Baghdad,
when he was five years old.
It is told concerning his composure,
that when the Caliph sent and clothed him in royal robes and seated him on the throne,
he stretched out neither his hand nor his foot,
nor did he blink his eyes,
nor did he lean or recline,
nor did he move any of his limbs,
but he sat thus like a rock,
so that everyone was astonished at him.
And she, Terken Khatun, took her son Sultan Mahmud,
and went to Isfahan.
Then others of the Turks gathered together,
and brought out the other son of Sultan Malik-Shah, who was born to him by his cousin,
the one whose name was Berkyaruq,
and made him king over them.
And there were ten thousand with him,
and with Mahmud his brother twenty thousand.
And when they met one another,
the nobles of Mahmud acted treacherously,
and crossed over to the side of Berkyaruq,
and were with him.
Also Taj al-Dawla Tutush,
the brother of Sultan Malik-Shah,
made himself king over Mosul, Nisibis, Mayperqat, and over Syria and Damascus.
And he came to Azerbaijan,
and Sultan Berkyaruq, his nephew, went to meet him,
and they met one another in the territory of Tabriz,
in a village named Saidabad.
And Tutush returned to Damascus,
and also Aq Sunqur and Buzan the amirs went into the service of Sultan Berkyaruq.
And that Berkyaruq went to Baghdad, and was received by the Caliph,
and he clothed him in royal robes,
and wrote a deed of investiture for him,
and proclaimed him sultan.
And in the year one thousand four hundred and eighty-seven of the Greeks [1176 AD],
487 of the Arabs [1094 AD],
while the Caliph al-Muqtadi was sitting at his table,
and eating from a roasted hen,
he had hallucinations.
And he said to the maidservant who was standing before him:
"Who are these who have entered upon us without permission?" And she turned behind her,
and saw no one.
And she turned back to him,
and saw him fallen on his back, gasping {OCR?}, before he had washed his hands.
And so he died suddenly,
and [al-Mustazhir] arose {OCR?}:
his son, sixteen years [old], his son al-Mustazhir {OCR?}.
After him, twenty-five [years] and five months {OCR?}.
And in this year died Terken Khatun, the mother of Sultan Mahmud.
This woman was brave and wise,
